name: PGPA ICT GOV Requirements
title: NDIA ICT Governance Policy — PGPA Act 2013 Requirements Register
preamble: NDIA ICT Governance Policy — PGPA Act 2013 Requirements Register
rows: The accountable authority must prepare an annual report for the entity in accordance with the PGPA Rule. The report is presented to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.

ICT Governance Policy to ensure ICT governance, cyber security posture, major ICT initiatives and significant ICT issues are appropriately disclosed in the NDIA Annual Report to the extent required. Reporting must be accurate and not misleading.

PGPA Rule Part 2 Division 3B prescribes annual report content. RMG 135 provides guidance. Significant ICT incidents or failures may be notifiable matters under s 19 and reportable in the Annual Report.

The accountable authority must ensure the entity has an audit committee with functions including reviewing the appropriateness of the entity's financial reporting, performance reporting, systems of risk oversight and management, and systems of internal control.

ICT Governance Policy to establish the Audit Committee's oversight role in relation to ICT risk, information security, and internal controls. ICT-related audit findings, cyber risk ratings and internal audit plans covering ICT domains must be reported to the Audit Committee.

PGPA Rule s 17 prescribes Audit Committee membership and functions. Audit Committee charter should explicitly reference ICT risk and cyber security as standing agenda items. Aligns with RMG 202 and ASX CGC Principles (adapted for CCEs).

The accountable authority must prepare annual performance statements for inclusion in the entity's annual report, reporting on the entity's performance against its purposes as set out in the Corporate Plan.

ICT Governance Policy to require that ICT-related performance data is captured and reported accurately to support the NDIA's Annual Performance Statements. ICT governance reports must be prepared in a timely manner to feed into the annual reporting cycle.
Annual performance statements are subject to ANAO audit (s 40). Accuracy of ICT performance data is critical. Aligns with RMG 131 (Annual Performance Statements).
The accountable authority must measure and assess the performance of the entity in achieving its purposes, in compliance with requirements prescribed by the PGPA Rule.

ICT Governance Policy to establish an ICT performance measurement framework with metrics aligned to NDIA purposes (e.g. system uptime, digital service delivery, cyber security maturity, ICT project delivery). Performance must be assessed against targets set in the Corporate Plan.
PGPA Rule Part 2A prescribes performance measure requirements (reliable, verifiable, unbiased). ICT KPIs must meet these criteria to be included in Annual Performance Statements.

The accountable authority must cause records to be kept that properly record and explain the entity's performance in achieving its purposes. Records must enable preparation of annual performance statements.

ICT Governance Policy to mandate maintenance of performance records relating to ICT activities, system availability, cyber incident metrics, and ICT project outcomes. Records must be kept in a form that supports preparation of Annual Performance Statements.
Interacts with the Archives Act 1983 (records retention) and PSPF information security requirements. ICT systems must support evidential quality of performance records.

The accountable authority must prepare a corporate plan at least once each reporting period covering the entity's purposes, operating environment, performance measures and activities, including for any subsidiaries. The plan must be given to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister.

ICT Governance Policy must require that ICT strategy and significant ICT initiatives are reflected in or aligned to the NDIA Corporate Plan. Major ICT investments, digital transformation programs and cyber resilience objectives should be included as performance measures in the Corporate Plan.
PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2 prescribes corporate plan content. Aligns with NDIA Digital Strategy. ICT governance should be an explicit topic in the Corporate Plan's operating context section.
Application of Government Policy Orders – Corporate CCEs
If a Government Policy Order applies to the NDIA, the accountable authority must ensure the order is complied with in relation to the entity and, so far as practicable, any subsidiary.

ICT Governance Framework
/ APS Policy Compliance

ICT Governance Policy must include a mechanism to monitor and comply with any Government Policy Orders that apply to NDIA's ICT environment (e.g. cloud-hosting policy directions, ASD-mandated controls). Non-compliance must be disclosed to the Minister under s 19.
Non-compliance with a GPO constitutes significant non-compliance with finance law (s 19 disclosure obligation). Monitor Finance Minister's GPO register.
Duty to Keep Responsible Minister and Finance Minister Informed

The accountable authority must: keep the responsible Minister informed of entity activities; provide reports, documents and information as required; notify the Minister of significant decisions; give reasonable notice of significant issues; and notify as soon as practicable after becoming aware of significant issues affecting the entity.

ICT Incident & Issues Management
/ ICT Governance Reporting

ICT Governance Policy must define what constitutes a 'significant' ICT issue (e.g. major cyber incident, system failure, significant data breach) and establish escalation procedures ensuring the CEO can fulfil this ministerial notification duty in a timely manner.

s 19(3) allows rules to prescribe 'significant' decision/issue criteria. Interacts with NDIA Crisis Management Framework, ASD cyber incident reporting (SOCI Act) and OAIC data breach notification obligations.
Duty to Govern the Commonwealth Entity

The accountable authority must govern the entity in a way that: (a) promotes the proper use and management of public resources; (b) promotes achievement of the entity's purposes; and (c) promotes financial sustainability.

ICT Governance Framework
/ ICT Resource Management

Ensure the ICT Governance Policy documents how ICT investments and resources are governed to promote proper use. The CEO (as accountable authority) must be reflected as the ultimate owner of ICT governance obligations.
s 15(2) also requires decisions to account for effect on public resources generally. ICT budget decisions must demonstrate alignment with this duty.
